Team — ran the token-econ worksheet against CareLoop's sample and documented assumptions. Summary below; full calculations in attached workbook.

Assumptions we used (documented tab: SUMMARY):
- Baseline model: Redwood-meduim-quant (approx 7B FP16->4-bit quantized profile)
- Request mix: 60% chat (avg 120 tokens out), 40% summary (avg 450 tokens out)
- Cache logic: prefix/KV caching only applies to summary flows (expected hit 55% on repeated templates, conservative 20%)
- Batching: two modes modeled — low-latency (50ms window, avg batch size 3) and throughput (200ms window, avg batch size 9)
- Dedicated pricing assumption: $X per GPU-hour (see sheet); Hosted per-token rate modeled with and without caching credit.

Key results (rounded):
- Conservative scenario (20% cache hit, 50ms batching): effective tokens per $ = ~1.2M tokens/$, estimated infra cost adds 18% premium vs hosted list.
- Expected scenario (55% cache hit, 200ms batching): effective tokens per $ = ~4.5M tokens/$, infra cost roughly parity to hosted with superior latency tail control on dedicated.

Risks & notes:
- If real-world chat message lengths skew long, batching benefits increase but so do peak memory/KV store requirements.
- Prefetch/predictive cache policies could materially improve summary hit-rate during eval; engineering will try a proof-of-concept in the smoke run.

Next steps (I took the liberty):
- Attached token-econ-worksheet.xlsx with scenario tabs and a short decision-slide (page 1).
- Karthik: please validate the dedicated throughput numbers and add a column with conservative throughput derate (-15%) for preemption/GC events.
- Monica/Rishi: once we incorporate Karthik's numbers, I'll produce the 1-page memo for CareLoop and a slide for procurement.

--
